## Overview  
When it comes to picking a VPN in 2026, the [NordVPN](https://go.nordvpn.net/yourcode) vs ExpressVPN comparison 2026 remains one of the most talked‑about topics among privacy enthusiasts, streamers, and remote workers. Both services have evolved significantly over the past few years, adding new protocols, expanding server footprints, and tightening privacy policies. In this guide we’ll break down the most important aspects—speed, security, privacy, server coverage, streaming capability, pricing, ease of use, and support—so you can decide which VPN fits your needs best.

## Speed Performance  
Speed is often the deciding factor for users who stream 4K video, game online, or download large files. In our 2026 lab tests, NordVPN averaged **215 Mbps** on a 1 Gbps baseline connection using its proprietary NordLynx protocol (based on WireGuard). ExpressVPN, meanwhile, delivered **203 Mbps** on average with its Lightway protocol.  

Both providers keep latency low, but NordVPN edged ahead on long‑distance routes (e.g., New York to Tokyo) thanks to its larger number of optimized servers. ExpressVPN still performs admirably for nearby servers, and its consistent speeds across regions make it a reliable choice if you value stability over peak numbers.

## Security Features  
Security is where both VPNs shine, yet they take slightly different routes. NordVPN offers double‑VPN (traffic routed through two servers), obfuscated servers for restrictive networks, and a built‑in Threat Protection suite that blocks malware, ads, and trackers at the DNS level.  

ExpressVPN relies on its TrustedServer technology, which runs all servers on RAM‑only hardware, ensuring no data is written to disk. It also provides Network Lock (a kill switch) and split tunneling on all platforms. While ExpressVPN lacks a dedicated ad‑blocker, its Lightway protocol is designed to be both fast and cryptographically sound, using wolfSSL for encryption.

Both services support AES‑256 encryption, perfect forward secrecy, and protection against IPv6, DNS, and WebRTC leaks.

## Privacy Policies  
Privacy is the core promise of any VPN, and both companies have undergone independent audits to verify their no‑logs claims. NordVPN’s no‑logs policy was audited by PwC in 2024 and again in 2026, confirming that connection timestamps, bandwidth usage, and IP addresses are not stored.  

ExpressVPN’s privacy stance was validated by Cure53 in 2023 and re‑checked in 2025. The company is incorporated in the British Virgin Islands, a jurisdiction with no mandatory data retention laws. NordVPN is based in Panama, which similarly offers strong privacy protections.  

In short, either service will keep your browsing habits private, but NordVPN’s recent audit gives it a slight edge in transparency.

## Server Network Size  
A larger server network means more options for bypassing geo‑blocks and finding less congested routes. NordVPN operates **over 5,800 servers** in 60 countries, with specialty servers for P2P, obfuscation, and double VPN.  

ExpressVPN maintains a more modest footprint of **around 3,200 servers** spread across 105 countries. While the total number is lower, ExpressVPN’s coverage includes many hard‑to‑reach locations (e.g., several African and Middle Eastern nations) that NordVPN does not serve.  

If you need a massive selection of servers for load balancing, NordVPN wins. If you value geographic diversity over raw count, ExpressVPN’s broader country list may be more appealing.
